summary.text: Amanda Janoo is the Democratic nominee for governor, an economist and first-time candidate who has worked in economic development for the United Nations and with the Wellbeing Economy Alliance.

She proposes higher taxes on top earners, second homes and large tech companies' digital advertising revenue; she says the income surcharge would fund free primary and preventive health care and second-home revenue would reduce property taxes.

paragraphs.text: Amanda Janoo was born on a farm in rural Vermont and raised in South Strafford; according to her campaign, her father immigrated from Malaysia and worked as a civil engineer.
She received a bachelor's degree in political science and global political economy from Macalester College in 2010 and a master of philosophy from the University of Cambridge in 2013.
Her campaign says she was awarded a Fulbright Scholarship for research with India's Self-Employed Women's Association and a Family Economic Security Fellowship with New America.
Janoo began her career working with the United Nations and international development organizations as an industrial policy and structural transformation specialist.

She is now economics and policy lead for the Wellbeing Economy Alliance, a global network, and according to her campaign has advised governments including Scotland, Wales, Finland, New Zealand and Canada.
In Vermont she co-founded the Wellbeing Economy Alliance of Vermont and has served on the boards of the ACLU of Vermont and Rights & Democracy Vermont.
Janoo rents an apartment in Burlington, which her campaign says is because she has been priced out of buying a home in the community where she grew up.
She won the Democratic nomination for governor in August 2026.
